## The architecture

The Transformer keeps the familiar **encoder-decoder** shape. The encoder turns the input tokens $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ into continuous vectors $z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)$. The decoder then produces the output $(y_1,\dots,y_m)$ one token at a time. It is **auto-regressive**: each token it has already generated is fed back in as input for the next.

The **encoder** is a stack of $N=6$ identical layers, each with two sub-layers: multi-head self-attention, then a small feed-forward network. Every sub-layer is wrapped as
$$\text{LayerNorm}(x + \text{Sublayer}(x)),$$
which is a residual connection (the input added back to the output) followed by layer normalization. The addition only works if input and output have the same size, so every sub-layer and embedding outputs vectors of $d_{\text{model}}=512$.

The **decoder** also has 6 layers, with a third sub-layer in the middle that attends over the encoder's output. Its self-attention is **masked** so that a position cannot attend to later positions. The target sequence is also fed in shifted right by one. Together these guarantee that the prediction for position $i$ uses only outputs before $i$. During training the whole target sentence is available at once, so without the mask the decoder could simply peek at the answer.
